a better understanding of the nature and severity of BPD in adolescents, and the development of more sensitive and specific diagnostic criteria for adolescent BPD.
a more comprehensive understanding and conceptualization of BPD in adolescence, to improve early detection and prevention of BPD in adolescents.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
adolescents with BPD, regardless of the number of criteria fulfilled, present with severe impairments and are in need of early detection and adequate treatment.
the clinical cut-off of 5 criteria should be lowered to 4 criteria, but that a lower cut-off should be considered for adolescents.
adolescents presenting with sub-threshold criteria for BPD and no current BPD should be considered at high risk for BPD and should be offered a comprehensive treatment program.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adolescents with subthreshold BPD are at-risk for developing a full-syndrom BPD and should be considered for early treatment.
subthreshold and full syndrome BPD in adolescents are associated with comparable levels of HRQoL impairment and psychopathological symptoms.
adolescents with sub-threshold or full-syndrom BPD should not be treated differently in the context of psychotherapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the clinical presentation of subthreshold and full BPD in adolescents does not differ in terms of self-reported psychosocial impairment and distress, which may have implications for the clinical utility of existing diagnostic criteria.
the diagnostic cut-off of BPD in adolescents may be lowered to 3 criteria to better identify those at-risk and to improve clinical utility.
adolescents with subthreshold BPD should be treated as early as possible, to avoid the progression to full-syddrome BPD and to reduce impairments in HRQL and psychopathological symptoms.
